dedupe_keys.name: noaa poes and metop space environment monitor sem particle data

description: The Space Environment Monitor instruments on the NOAA POES and EUMETSAT MetOp polar-orbiting satellites measure the flux of energetic ions and electrons at about 850 km altitude. The Total Energy Detector measures the energy flux of auroral protons and electrons entering the polar atmosphere, and the Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector monitors protons and electrons from 30 keV to more than 200 MeV, covering radiation-belt particles, solar proton events and low-energy cosmic rays. The collection holds Level 0b raw counts from SEM-1 and SEM-2 since November 1978 and NCEI-derived Level 1a count rates and Level 1b fluxes since January 2012, plus a Level 2 product for July 1998 to December 2014. The NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center uses the data to monitor the near-Earth environment. Files are accessible free from the NCEI HTTPS server as daily or monthly NetCDF and binary files with a processing manual. Caveats: detectors degrade and suffer proton contamination of electron channels, instruments and satellites change over the record, and users must pick the right processing level. It supports radiation-environment inputs for satellite anomaly attribution, aviation radiation and HF absorption models; related records are CDAWeb and the NOAA SWPC products.
name: NOAA POES and MetOp Space Environment Monitor (SEM) particle data
notes: The 850 km altitude is the nominal POES orbit and is not stated on the pages read; licence is inferred from NOAA's usual public-domain status.
provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), with NOAA NESDIS and EUMETSAT

sources.note: TED and MEPED, 30 keV to >200 MeV, L0b since Nov 1978, L1a/L1b since Jan 2012, L2 Jul 1998-Dec 2014, NetCDF and binary, HTTPS direct download, SEM-2 processing manual, SWPC use
